docs.text: Driver ADS7952 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the TI ADS7950, ADS7951, ADS7952 and ADS7953 12-bit SAR ADCs. It checks that the chip really answers, reads channels one at a time or as a scan with the fewest frames the chip allows, and keys every result on the channel address in its reply, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves one 16-bit frame at a time; it does the rest: the reset, the identity check, the frame pipeline, the program sequences and the checks. 12-bit SAR ADC ADS7952 Texas Instruments Function 12 single-ended channels (4, 8 or 16 on the ADS7950, ADS7951, ADS7953), 12 bits, up to 1 MSPS Interface SPI mode 0, up to 20 MHz; one 16-bit frame per conversion, the result two frames after its channel Modes Manual (any channel per frame), Auto-1 (a programmed list), Auto-2 (channel 0 to a last channel) Ranges 0 to VREF or 0 to 2 x VREF, with an external 2.0 V to 3.0 V reference Extras Two alarm thresholds per channel on GPIO0 and GPIO1; four GPIOs (TSSOP); power-down Supply +VA 2.7 V to 5.25 V, +VBD 1.7 V to +VA What you get ¶ One object per chip. ADS7952<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . A start-up check a dead bus cannot pass. Two channels selected, their addresses read back two frames later: MISO stuck, a fixed pattern or an SDI that never reaches the chip all fail. See Contract . The minimum traffic. A running Auto-1 scan costs one frame per channel; a repeated channel one frame. Extra read-backs are chosen per call. See Contract . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as Bus , ChannelMismatch or SequenceMismatch . See API guide . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: a transfer and a delay, plus an optional logging hook. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . See Contract . Tested without hardware. Host tests run the driver against a protocol model of the chip with the faults seen on hardware, and a fuzzer attacks every reply. See Testing and CI and Status and limitations . docs.text: API guide ¶ How to use each part of the ADS7952 driver: start it, read channels one at a time or as a scan, change the range, the sequences, the alarms and the GPIOs, and handle every error. Every snippet compiles in the host build. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SLAS605 C: Power-down through DI05: 8.3.2 Power Saving, p. 29 Manual mode and the two-frame read latency: 8.4.4 Operating in Manual Mode, Figures 50 and 51, Table 1, p. 31 Auto-1 mode and its program register: 8.4.5 Operating in Auto-1 Mode, Figures 52 to 54, Tables 2 to 4, p. 34 Auto-2 mode and its program register: 8.4.6 Operating in Auto-2 Mode, Figures 55 to 57, Tables 5 and 6, p. 38 Output codes and the LSB size: 8.5.1 Digital Output, Table 8, p. 41 GPIO program register and the register reset: 8.5.2 GPIO Registers, Figure 58, Table 11, p. 42 Alarm thresholds: 8.5.3 Alarm Thresholds for GPIO Pins, Figure 59, Tables 12 and 13, p. 43 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ Group Calls Lifecycle EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , Deinitialize() , ApplyConfig() , GetConfig() Conversions ReadChannel() , ReadChannels() , ReadAuto1() , ReadAuto2() , TraceFrames() Settings SetRange() , SetAuto1Channels() , SetAuto2LastChannel() , SetAlarmThresholds() , SetGpioOutputs() , ReadGpio() No I/O GetChannelCount() , ToMicrovolts() , GetLastReply() ; free: Validate() , ResetConfig() , CodeToMicrovolts() , ChannelCount() , reg::ReplyAddress() , reg::ReplyCode() Every call that can fail returns ads7952::Result<T> : check ok() (or the bool conversion), then read value . The Contract page gives the frames each call sends. Start ¶ ads7952 :: Error BringUp ( Adc & adc ) { // The one entry point: resets and checks the chip on the first call, then returns Ok with no // I/O. After a failure the next call starts again from the beginning. const auto r = adc . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "ADS7952 init: %s (last reply 0x%04X) \n " , ads7952 :: ToString ( r . error ), static_cast < unsigned > ( adc . GetLastReply ())); } return r . error ; } EnsureInitialized() is the one way to start. Its first call checks the configuration, brings the bus up, resets the chip through the GPIO program register, writes every program register and the range, and checks that the replies carry the channel addresses it selected ( Contract ). After it succeeds, later calls return Ok with no I/O; after it fails, the next call starts again from the reset. Deinitialize() powers the chip down; Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() is the full restart. Read one channel or a list ¶ ReadChannel(ch) converts one channel in Manual mode. A new channel costs three frames (select, acquire, return); the same channel again costs one, because the chip keeps converting the channel it was given. ads7952 :: Error ReadThree ( Adc & adc , std :: array < uint16_t , 3 >& codes ) { const std :: array < uint8_t , 3 > channels { 4 , 7 , 9 }; // Figure 51: 3 + 2 frames return adc . ReadChannels ( channels , codes ). error ; } ReadChannels(list, codes) pipelines the selects as the datasheet's Figure 51 does: list length + 2 frames for the whole list, against three per channel with ReadChannel() . Repeats are allowed. Both calls check the address of every reply and return ChannelMismatch instead of a result for another channel, or DeviceReset when the reply came from channel 0, the channel a reset puts the chip on; after either the driver must be started again. Scan a sequence: the hot path ¶ // A control loop: the same channels every tick. The first call enters Auto-1 (k + 2 frames), // every later one is k frames (one Auto-1 word per channel). ads7952 :: Error Tick ( Adc & adc , std :: array < uint16_t , 16 >& codes ) { const auto bank = adc . ReadAuto1 (); if ( ! bank ) { return bank . error ; // DeviceReset or SequenceMismatch: call EnsureInitialized() again } codes = bank . value . code ; // codes[ch] for every ch in bank.value.mask return ads7952 :: Error :: Ok ; } ReadAuto1() returns one pass of the Auto-1 sequence ( Config::auto1_channels ) in a Bank : code[ch] for every ch in mask . While the chip runs the sequence, a pass of k channels is k frames, the minimum the chip allows: each is the Auto-1 word with DI11 = 1 and no restart, which re-sends the range (a "continue" word would not). The first call, or the first after a manual read, enters Auto-1 with one more frame and skips the reply in flight (k + 2). The replies must be one turn of the sequence in the chip's order, starting anywhere: anything else is SequenceMismatch ( DeviceReset for a reply from channel 0 out of turn), and the driver must be started again. ReadAuto2() does the same for channel 0 to Config::auto2_last_channel . ads7952 :: Error UseChannels ( Adc & adc , uint16_t mask ) { // Two frames, plus one scan that checks the chip took the new list; the scan leaves the // sequence running, so the next ReadAuto1() costs one frame per channel. return adc . SetAuto1Channels ( mask , ads7952 :: Verify :: ReadBack ). error ; } SetAuto1Channels(mask) writes the mask (two frames). Call it when the list changes, not before every pass: the chip keeps it until a reset. With Verify::ReadBack it scans once and checks the addresses are the new sequence ( WriteMismatch otherwise), which also leaves the sequence running for the next ReadAuto1() . A DMA stream that sends "continue" words by itself can take over once the sequence runs: decode each word with reg::ReplyAddress() and reg::ReplyCode() , and key results on the address. When the stream stops, the next ReadAuto1() checks the replies and enters the mode again only if the chip left it. Range and conversion to volts ¶ SetRange(range) sends one mode word with the new DI06. Results from the second frame after it use the new range; the next conversion call skips the one in between by itself. Range 2 (0 to 2 x VREF) is only allowed while 2 x vref_mv <= va_min_mv (section 7.6). With GPIO2 as the range input, the pin selects the range and SetRange() returns Unsupported . ToMicrovolts(code) converts with the configured range and reference: one LSB is full scale / 4096 (Table 8). ToMicrovolts(bank, channel) converts with Bank::range , the range the scan was made in, so a bank kept across SetRange() still converts right. CodeToMicrovolts(code, range, vref_mv) does the same without a driver object. Proving the scale ¶ The chip cannot report its range, and a lost range doubles or halves every code while every address still checks out. Declare a channel that carries a voltage derived from REFP in Config::monitor : EnsureInitialized() checks it once (3 frames), CheckScale() checks it on demand (1 to 3 frames), and CheckScaleCode(code) judges a code you already have, such as the monitor's entry of each bank, with no frame at all. They return RangeMismatch when the code is what the other range gives and ScaleMismatch when neither range explains it. How to wire the monitor, choose the range for a supply and decode ratiometric sensors: Reference, range and supplies . Alarms ¶ ads7952 :: Error ArmOverRange ( Adc & adc ) { // GPIO0 goes high when channel 0 reads above 3600 or below 400 (Config::gpio.alarm_output must // be AlarmOutput::Gpio0HighOrLow). The chip keeps the upper 10 bits of each threshold. return adc . SetAlarmThresholds ( 0 , { 400 , 3600 }). error ; } SetAlarmThresholds(ch, {low, high}) writes both thresholds of one channel in four frames. The chip keeps the upper 10 bits of each and compares them with the upper 10 bits of every result of that channel, in every mode. The alarm reaches a pin only when Config::gpio.alarm_output routes it there. Thresholds cannot be read back; set them all at once in Config::alarms and EnsureInitialized() writes every group that differs from the reset value. GPIOs ¶ ads7952 :: Error Indicate ( Adc & adc , bool on ) { // Config::gpio.output_mask must make GPIO2 an output. ReadBack: one more frame, and the level // is read back from the pin. const auto levels = static_cast < uint8_t > ( on ? 0x04U : 0x00U ); return adc . SetGpioOutputs ( levels , ads7952 :: Verify :: ReadBack ). error ; } Config::gpio sets each pin's direction and function. SetGpioOutputs(levels) drives the output pins: a mode word with the new levels and the frame on whose CS falling edge the chip drives them, so the pins have changed when it returns. Verify::ReadBack adds one frame and reads the levels back from the pins ( WriteMismatch when a pin does not follow, for example one held by the board). ReadGpio() reads all four levels in two frames. Bring-up trace ¶ // Bring-up: is SDI reaching the chip? The address nibble of words[2] onwards must be 11. bool SdiReachesChip ( ads7952 :: ADS7952 < FullPort >& adc ) { std :: array < uint16_t , 6 > words {}; if ( ! adc . TraceFrames ( 11 , words )) { return false ; } return ads7952 :: reg :: ReplyAddress ( words [ 5 ]) == 11 ; } TraceFrames(ch, words) selects a channel and returns every reply word unparsed. From words[2] on, the address nibble must be the channel; a nibble that never follows means SDI does not reach the chip. For bring-up and fault finding the driver keeps what it saw and offers one raw access (handbook KB-CPP-129): Call I/O What it gives TraceFrames(ch, words) words.size() frames, one shot, no retry, no check of the replies Every reply word unparsed. Its one side effect: the chip is left in Manual mode on ch , as after ReadChannel(ch) GetLastReply() none The last reply word of any call, the driver's own frames included; 0xFFFF before the first and after a failed transfer There is no status latch (handbook KB-CPP-119) because the chip has no clear-on-read or write-1-to-clear flag: a reply carries only the channel address (or the GPIO levels) and the code, and the alarm outputs are pins that the chip sets on the 12 th SCLK falling edge of a frame and clears on the 10 th of the next (section 8.1), with nothing to read back. Use it from a handler ¶ On a board, the driver sits under a handler that owns it, the port and the bus. The driver leaves to the handler what it cannot know: When to probe. Never from a static constructor or at boot: an unplugged board leaves MISO floating, and the bus is shared. Construct the driver at boot if you like (it does no I/O), call EnsureInitialized() from the attach path, and on each attach start again with Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() . The shared bus. The driver takes no lock and never configures the bus. Take the bus lock around each call and pause other traffic on the bus for its duration. The scan. Write the channel list once ( SetAuto1Channels() , or Config::auto1_channels before the start), then call ReadAuto1() every tick. Do not write the mask before every pass: two frames per pass for nothing. Board-level checks. The driver proves the address of every result. Declare VREF_MON as Config::monitor and judge it in every bank with CheckScaleCode() : that catches a lost range word and a reset during a running sequence at no frame cost. Check also for a bank whose counts are all identical; it catches a broken front end (with SDI not reaching the chip, every count once read 0x0E83). Retries. The driver never retries. What to do on each error: Error In the start In a read or a scan In a setting NoDevice Board absent or unpowered: report it, probe again on the next attach DeviceIdMismatch SDI, MISO or CS broken, or another part: report, do not use ChannelMismatch EnsureInitialized() (the driver is uninitialised) SequenceMismatch EnsureInitialized() (the driver is uninitialised) DeviceReset The chip was reset: EnsureInitialized() re-arms alarms and GPIOs WriteMismatch GPIO: a pin held by the board. Sequence: restart Bus The port failed: check the bus, then probe again Same Same; the chip may hold part of the setting ( IsConfigUncertain() ): ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( ads7952 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case ads7952 :: Error :: Bus : case ads7952 :: Error :: NoDevice : case ads7952 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "check the wiring: SDI, SDO, SCLK, CS and the supplies" ; case ads7952 :: Error :: DeviceReset : case ads7952 :: Error :: ChannelMismatch : case ads7952 :: Error :: SequenceMismatch : return "the chip was reset or a frame was lost: call EnsureInitialized()" ; default : return ads7952 :: ToString ( e ); } } Signal Meaning What to do Error::NoDevice At start-up every reply was 0xFFFF: nothing drives MISO Board plugged and powered? CS and SDO wiring Error::DeviceIdMismatch At start-up the replies did not follow the selects Address 0 every time: SDI not reaching the chip, or MISO stuck low. Run TraceFrames() Error::DeviceReset A reply came from channel 0 out of turn, or the monitor reads Range 1: the chip was reset The driver is uninitialised; EnsureInitialized() programs the chip again. Check +VA under load Error::ChannelMismatch A reply carried another channel's address A lost frame: the driver is uninitialised; EnsureInitialized() Error::SequenceMismatch An Auto pass was not one turn of the sequence The chip left the mode or lost its mask: EnsureInitialized() Error::WriteMismatch A read-back differed A GPIO pin held by the board, or a program frame lost Error::RangeMismatch The scale monitor reads what the other range gives Do not publish the bank. Check the GPIO2 strap; restart, which resets the chip and checks again Error::ScaleMismatch The scale monitor fits neither range Do not publish. REFP missing or not settled, or the monitor channel not wired as declared Error::Unsupported A GPIO the VQFN lacks, or SetRange() with GPIO2 as range input Fix the Config Error::Bus The port failed a transfer or the bus bring-up Check the port and the wiring Error::InvalidArgument A Config field or an argument is out of range; nothing was sent Fix the value ( Validate() , GetChannelCount() ) Error::NotInitialized EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded Call it ads7952 :: Error Recover ( Adc & adc ) { // After DeviceReset, ChannelMismatch or SequenceMismatch (the driver is then uninitialised), or a // reference monitor that reads wrong: power down, then reset and write every register again. ( void ) adc . Deinitialize (); return adc . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } Error::Timeout , Error::Crc , Error::Busy and Error::DeviceFault belong to the shared base set but are never returned by this driver: no call waits for the chip, which sends no CRC, is never busy and reports no fault. Every value, with the calls that return it, is on the Contract page. ads7952::ToString() names an error for a log. Next: Configuration .

docs.text: On a board, the driver sits under a handler that owns it, the port and the bus. The driver leaves to the handler what it cannot know: When to probe. Never from a static constructor or at boot: an unplugged board leaves MISO floating, and the bus is shared. Construct the driver at boot if you like (it does no I/O), call EnsureInitialized() from the attach path, and on each attach start again with Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() . The shared bus. The driver takes no lock and never configures the bus. Take the bus lock around each call and pause other traffic on the bus for its duration. The scan. Write the channel list once ( SetAuto1Channels() , or Config::auto1_channels before the start), then call ReadAuto1() every tick. Do not write the mask before every pass: two frames per pass for nothing. Board-level checks. The driver proves the address of every result. Declare VREF_MON as Config::monitor and judge it in every bank with CheckScaleCode() : that catches a lost range word and a reset during a running sequence at no frame cost. Check also for a bank whose counts are all identical; it catches a broken front end (with SDI not reaching the chip, every count once read 0x0E83). Retries. The driver never retries. What to do on each error: Error In the start In a read or a scan In a setting NoDevice Board absent or unpowered: report it, probe again on the next attach DeviceIdMismatch SDI, MISO or CS broken, or another part: report, do not use ChannelMismatch EnsureInitialized() (the driver is uninitialised) SequenceMismatch EnsureInitialized() (the driver is uninitialised) DeviceReset The chip was reset: EnsureInitialized() re-arms alarms and GPIOs WriteMismatch GPIO: a pin held by the board. Sequence: restart Bus The port failed: check the bus, then probe again Same Same; the chip may hold part of the setting ( IsConfigUncertain() ): ApplyConfig(GetConfig())

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one of them yours, and what happens in each when you read a channel. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SLAS605 C: Frame, reply word, GPIO refresh and alarm timing: 8.1 Overview, p. 28 Manual mode and the two-frame read latency: 8.4.4 Operating in Manual Mode, Figures 50 and 51, Table 1, p. 31 Auto-1 mode and its program register: 8.4.5 Operating in Auto-1 Mode, Figures 52 to 54, Tables 2 to 4, p. 34 The "continue" word: 8.4.7 Continued Operation in a Selected Mode, Table 7, p. 41 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/ads7952.hpp public calls ; inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . In each panel the top row is the word the driver sends on SDI, the middle row the channel the multiplexer acquires during that frame, and the bottom row the reply on SDO: the conversion of the channel acquired in the frame before, sampled at this frame's CS falling edge, tagged with its address in DO15:12. In Manual mode (top) ReadChannel(4) selects channel 4 with a Manual word, sends a "continue" word and then the Manual word for channel 4 again (it carries the range once more), and keeps the third reply, whose address must be 4; the two replies before it still belong to the previous channel. In Auto-1 (bottom), entering the mode restarts the sequence at its first channel: with channels 2, 5 and 6 programmed, the first result arrives two frames after the Auto-1 word, and from then on every Auto-1 word without restart (DI11 = 1, the range again) returns the next channel of the sequence, so a pass costs one frame per channel. The timing is the datasheet's Figures 51 and 53; the frame counts come from ReadChannel(), readSelected(), scan() and collect() in src/ads7952.ipp. Drawn from: src/ads7952.ipp select() ; src/ads7952.ipp selectChecked() ; src/ads7952.ipp readSelected() ; src/ads7952.ipp scan() ; inc/ads7952_registers.hpp kContinue ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/frame-pipeline.py . The chip answers each frame with the result of the channel the frame before last chose (Figures 51 and 53). The core keeps three facts so that each call sends the fewest frames and returns only results that belong to it: the mode the chip is in (Manual, Auto-1, Auto-2, or unknown after a failure), the Manual channel, and how many replies still in flight were acquired before its last change (a select, an Auto entry, a new range or sequence). A read that does not need to choose the channel lets those replies pass; any other read chooses it again, which also sends the range. A reply's address is always checked against the channel it must carry. Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the SpiPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Optional hooks by named concepts. DelayUs and Log are detected by HasDelayUs and HasLog in one place, which match the hook's address against exactly one noexcept signature ( detail::ExactHook ). A missing DelayUs() fails to compile, and so does a hook declared with another signature; a missing Log() logs nothing. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail and clocks nothing, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler built at boot, before the board is plugged in. Key every result on its address. The chip tags each reply with its channel; the driver never infers a channel from frame counting alone. A lost frame, a reset chip or a deaf SDI line becomes an error, not a wrong value. Minimum frames, extra checks per call. The hot path sends one mode word per result; the read-backs the chip allows (GPIO levels, the scanned sequence) are asked for per call with Verify::ReadBack . No mode calls. The driver enters Manual, Auto-1 or Auto-2 when a read needs it; the caller never has to keep the chip's mode and the driver's view in step. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state. docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries under Breaking need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Changed ¶ The repository moved to kokeb-labs-drivers; URLs follow. The Hardware page draws the chip from the new docs/hardware.yml : the TSSOP-38 pinout with each pin's port hook, the functional block diagram of section 8.2, the typical application of Figure 60 with its reference, supply and input capacitors, and the pin and parts tables, every fact with its datasheet section and page. The example supply voltages and the reference's own supply are marked as not confirmed. The hand-written pin table is gone. The hardware-lessons-review skill and tools/preflight.sh follow the template. [0.1.0] - 2026-11-09 ¶ Breaking ¶ A reply the driver cannot account for now leaves a running driver uninitialised: after ChannelMismatch , SequenceMismatch , the new Error::DeviceReset (22), a WriteMismatch from a sequence read-back, or a failed CheckScale() (other than Bus ), every call returns NotInitialized until EnsureInitialized() succeeds again. A mismatching reply from channel 0, the power-on channel (section 8.4.3), and a CheckScale() that finds Range 1 where the driver sends Range 2 are DeviceReset instead of ChannelMismatch , SequenceMismatch or RangeMismatch . Handle DeviceReset and call EnsureInitialized() after any of these errors. ApplyConfig() on a running driver writes every register, changed or not (6 + 10 frames per alarm group, 36 on the ADS7952), instead of the differences from its own copy. Added ¶ IsConfigUncertain() : true after a setter or ApplyConfig() failed with Bus , or a Verify::ReadBack did not confirm the write (the frame may have reached the chip), until every register is written again: ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) , or Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() . GetConfig() keeps the values last written successfully; alarm thresholds are never assumed set after a failed write. Config::park_channel (opt-in, kNoPark by default): after ReadChannel(0) the chip rests on this channel, so a reset while it would otherwise rest on channel 0, the power-on channel, shows as DeviceReset at the next read. ReadChannel(0) costs one frame more (4 when repeated). First version of the driver for the TI ADS7950, ADS7951, ADS7952 and ADS7953 12-bit SPI SAR ADCs, written on the driver template against datasheet SLAS605C. ads7952::ADS7952<Port> with the configuration in the constructor and one start-up call, EnsureInitialized() : two frames that end any open program sequence, a register reset through the GPIO program register, every program register written, and an identity check that selects two channels and demands their addresses back (a, a, b), which a stuck or patterned MISO, an echo and a deaf SDI cannot pass. ApplyConfig() writes only what changed; Deinitialize() powers the chip down. Conversions keyed on the channel address of every reply: ReadChannel() (1 to 3 frames), ReadChannels() (pipelined, list length + 2 frames), ReadAuto1() and ReadAuto2() (one frame per channel while the sequence runs), TraceFrames() for bring-up. Error::ChannelMismatch and Error::SequenceMismatch . Settings: SetRange() (the next read skips the old-range reply), SetAuto1Channels() , SetAuto2LastChannel() , SetAlarmThresholds() , SetGpioOutputs() , ReadGpio() ; Verify::ReadBack per call reads back the GPIO levels or scans the new sequence ( Error::WriteMismatch ). Config with the reset value of every register, the variant, the package, the reference and the lowest guaranteed +VA ( va_min_mv ); a constexpr Validate() (Range 2 only while 2 x VREF <= va_min_mv ), ResetConfig() , CodeToMicrovolts() (one LSB is full scale / 4096); Kconfig options for the part, package, range, voltages and sequences. A scale monitor: Config::monitor declares a channel with a voltage derived from REFP. EnsureInitialized() checks it once (3 frames), CheckScale() on demand, and CheckScaleCode() judges a code already read, such as the monitor's entry of each Bank , with no frame. Error::RangeMismatch (the chip converts in the other range: a GPIO2 strap or a reset) and Error::ScaleMismatch (the reference or the monitor input is wrong). Validate() refuses a monitor that cannot tell the two ranges apart. Bank::range and ToMicrovolts(bank, channel) : a scan always converts with the range it was made in. The "Reference, range and supplies" page: how a code becomes a voltage, choosing VREF and the range for a supply, the scale monitor, ratiometric sensors decoded against their measured supply, power and layout from the datasheet, a board checklist and a worked example of a 5 V sensor board. After a failed frame inside a program sequence the driver repeats the Auto-1 mask or closes the alarm sequence, so the chip never takes the next command as data (found by the bus-fault sweep and the fuzzer). Host tests over a protocol model of the four parts with the bus and board faults a real board can produce, every frame of every operation failed in turn; a libFuzzer target with its corpus replayed as a CTest; the host and ESP32 examples; the frame-pipeline figure. Not verified on hardware. docs/limitations.md : the design choices with the datasheet section each rests on, the limits of the design, what the model cannot show, and the bench steps to run before depending on the driver. Changed ¶ The misra-review , cpp20-profile and new-driver-from-template skills and docs/repo-setup.md follow the template: reading the MISRA report, the known tool misfires, enumeration ranges without a sentinel, and the settings tool. tools/preflight.sh and the verify and hardware-lessons-review skills follow the template: every check CI runs that a workstation can run, in one command, and the rules for device resets, faults the chip clears itself, dropped writes, switch-offs that no uncertainty refuses and a model that changes state on its own. The port concepts match each hook's address against exactly one noexcept signature with detail::ExactHook<Port, Sig>::Take(&Port::Hook) instead of probing it with a converting detail::Exactly<T> : no conversion operator is left. A misdeclared hook is still a compile error. kAlwaysFalse takes a class and the enumeration helpers an enumeration ( ClassType , Enumeration ), each with a compile-fail test. The cpp20-profile skill is the template's again. The repository documents only this driver against its datasheet: each design choice cites the datasheet section it rests on (or states its reasoning and a bench step), with no dated history. The copyright holder is The driver-ads7952 authors in LICENSE , every source header, driver.yml ( authors ) and the docs footer. tools/check_standalone.py , from the driver template, checks both in the repository checks. The driver follows the current handbook rules and the C++20 profile, from the driver template: Every header has an #ifndef include guard named after its file (KB-CPP-019); no #pragma is left. The bus requirements are constexpr in inc/ads7952_spi_interface.hpp (KB-CPP-123): kSpiMode 0, kMsbFirst , kMaxClockHz 20 MHz, kMinCsHighNs 20 (t_w1), kCsSetupNs 8 (t_su1), kCsHoldNs 0, kQuietNs 40 (t_q), kSdoReleaseNs 26 (t_d3), kContinuousWord and kFrameBits 16, from datasheet sections 7.3, 7.9 and 8.1. The host and ESP32 ports check their settings with static_assert , and the ESP32 port refuses a clock above the limit and drives CS high before it enables the pin (KB-HW-018). SpiPort checks each hook's exact parameter types, noexcept and bool result (KB-CPP20-006): a port whose Transfer() takes a narrower length or is not noexcept no longer compiles. DelayUs and Log are found by the named concepts HasDelayUs and HasLog , and a hook declared with another signature is a compile error (KB-CPP20-007). Compile-fail tests for each case. Error is [[nodiscard]] (KB-CPP20-037), and so are the pure helpers. GetConfig() is & -qualified and deleted on a temporary driver (KB-CPP20-044). Every target builds as ISO C++20 ( CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF , -pedantic-errors , the C++20 deprecations as errors); ads7952_header_checks compiles each public header alone on GCC, Clang and the Cortex-M cross-build, and examples/esp32/main/ads7952_cxx20_check.cpp does the same inside the ESP-IDF build. The tests and fuzzers build with the standard library's assertions. Bit work is in uint32_t , with every shift count masked or proved below the width (KB-CPP20-020, -021): no unsigned long or UL shifts (64 bits on the host, 32 on the targets), no promoted uint8_t or uint16_t operand of a shift, ~ , | or ^ , and no compound assignment that narrows (KB-CPP20-022). <bit> counts and rotates the channel masks ( std::popcount , std::rotr , std::countr_zero ). ToString(Error) is a switch over every enumerator; Validate() checks enumerations with detail::IsEnumerator() ; loops have no extra flag in their condition. The frame builders, the GPIO and mode encoders (now free constexpr functions), the reset configurations, the channel helpers, the identity channels and the code-to-voltage conversion are proved with static_assert against the datasheet tables. The two frame buffers belong to the driver object instead of the call's stack. The chip model ( tests/mock_ads7952.hpp ) includes no driver header: it has its own frame format, reset values, channel counts and power-up time with their datasheet sections, and tests/test_model.cpp checks them against the driver's at compile time (KB-TST-030). TraceFrames() documents its side effect (the chip is left in Manual mode on the channel); the API guide lists the raw access, and the Status page lists the handbook rules the chip gives no handle for (no clear-on-read flag to latch, no ready bit, 0x0000 being a valid channel 0 reply). The template's review skills ( cpp20-profile , misra-review , hardware-lessons-review ), the safety-reviewer agent, the updated verify skill and the Handbook source checks CI job, pinned at the handbook's C++20-profile commit; _config/.clang-tidy follows the handbook. The frame cost of every call is unchanged. CI runs fewer jobs, from the driver template: the host tests build GCC and Clang in one job; DCO, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the handbook rules, template drift and cppcheck are steps of one Repository checks job ( ci-repo-checks.yml , replacing ci-handbook.yml , ci-cpp-analysis.yml , ci-markdown-lint.yml and ci-yaml-lint.yml ); cross-compile and host quality use ci-tools' one-job layouts. docs.text: Contract ¶ What the ADS7952 driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Datasheet sections this page relies on From Texas Instruments SLAS605 C: Input ranges, power-up time and the invalid first conversion: 7.6 Electrical Characteristics (ADS7950 to ADS7953), p. 12 Frame, reply word, GPIO refresh and alarm timing: 8.1 Overview, p. 28 Power-down through DI05: 8.3.2 Power Saving, p. 29 Power-up and the programming sequence: 8.4.3 Device Power-Up Sequence, Figure 49, p. 30 GPIO program register and the register reset: 8.5.2 GPIO Registers, Figure 58, Table 11, p. 42 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , does no I/O and cannot fail. No call clocks the bus before EnsureInitialized() , so the driver can be constructed statically even where MISO may float. EnsureInitialized() resets the chip, writes the configuration and runs the identity check below. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised, and the next call starts again from the reset. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds and sends nothing. No call starts the chip as a side effect. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus . A failed call returns T{} ; a failed ReadChannels() or TraceFrames() leaves its buffer zeroed, never a partial result. A result is returned only from a reply whose address (DO15:12) is the channel it stands for, two frames after the frame that chose the channel (Figures 51, 53, 56). A Manual reply with another address is ChannelMismatch ; an Auto-1 or Auto-2 pass that is not one turn of the sequence is SequenceMismatch ; either one from channel 0, the power-on channel (section 8.4.3), is DeviceReset . The replies a select or an Auto entry discards must carry the Manual channel the chip had settled on. After DeviceReset , ChannelMismatch , SequenceMismatch from a running driver, or a failed CheckScale() (other than Bus ), the driver is uninitialised: it never writes again from a configuration the chip may have lost, and EnsureInitialized() resets and programs it again (fail-safe). A reply converted in the old range after SetRange() is never returned: the next read skips it. Every mode word the driver sends has DI11 = 1 and carries the configured range and GPIO levels, with DI04 = 0 and DI05 = 0 (except Deinitialize() 's), so a chip reset behind the driver's back gets them back at the next read, select or Auto entry. The frame that returns a ReadChannel() result is such a Manual word. ApplyConfig() on a running driver writes every register, whatever the driver's copy says. A setter or ApplyConfig() that fails with Bus (or a Verify::ReadBack that does not confirm the write) leaves GetConfig() at the values last written successfully and IsConfigUncertain() true, until ApplyConfig() or EnsureInitialized() writes every register again. Calls send only the frames the datasheet needs; the table under Timing gives each count. Extra verification is chosen per call with Verify::ReadBack and adds the frames stated there. A failed frame inside a program sequence (the Auto-1 mask, an alarm group) is followed by a frame that ends the sequence, so the chip never takes the next command as data; EnsureInitialized() also opens with two such frames. The replies of frames 3, 4 and 5 must carry addresses a , a and b (the result of a select comes back two frames later and the chip keeps converting the selected channel, Figure 51). docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a simulated ADS7952, through the host port host_ads7952_port.hpp . No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/ads7952_host_example The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest ads7952_host_example ). ESP32 ¶ ESP-IDF applications that run the driver on an ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the port in esp32_ads7952_port.hpp . The project points EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at the repository root, which is the driver's ESP-IDF component. The acquisition time is 325 ns minimum (section 7.6), and with MXO shorted to AINP the source impedance should be 50 Ω or less, since a higher one slows settling after a channel change (section 9.1.1). The frame ¶ A result comes back two frames after its channel Figure description and sources Each column is one 16-bit frame, CS low for 16 SCLK cycles, left to right in time. In each panel the top row is the word the driver sends on SDI, the middle row the channel the multiplexer acquires during that frame, and the bottom row the reply on SDO: the conversion of the channel acquired in the frame before, sampled at this frame's CS falling edge, tagged with its address in DO15:12. In Manual mode (top) ReadChannel(4) selects channel 4 with a Manual word, sends a "continue" word and then the Manual word for channel 4 again (it carries the range once more), and keeps the third reply, whose address must be 4; the two replies before it still belong to the previous channel. In Auto-1 (bottom), entering the mode restarts the sequence at its first channel: with channels 2, 5 and 6 programmed, the first result arrives two frames after the Auto-1 word, and from then on every Auto-1 word without restart (DI11 = 1, the range again) returns the next channel of the sequence, so a pass costs one frame per channel. The timing is the datasheet's Figures 51 and 53; the frame counts come from ReadChannel(), readSelected(), scan() and collect() in src/ads7952.ipp. Drawn from: src/ads7952.ipp select() ; src/ads7952.ipp selectChecked() ; src/ads7952.ipp readSelected() ; src/ads7952.ipp scan() ; inc/ads7952_registers.hpp kContinue ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/frame-pipeline.py . Each frame is one 16-bit word in and one out, MSB first. The word in (DI15:00) has its command in DI15:12: DI15:12 Word Driver use 0000 Continue in the current mode; DI11:00 ignored (Table 7) Every frame that only reads 0001 Manual mode, next channel in DI10:07 (Table 1) ReadChannel() , ReadChannels() , the identity check 0010, 0011 Auto-1, Auto-2 mode (Tables 2, 5) ReadAuto1() , ReadAuto2() 0100 GPIO program register (Table 11) Start-up reset, GpioConfig 1000 Auto-1 program: the mask follows in the next frame (Table 3) SetAuto1Channels() 1001 Auto-2 program: last channel in DI09:06 (Table 6) SetAuto2LastChannel() 11bb Alarm program, group bb; thresholds follow (Table 13) SetAlarmThresholds() In a mode word, DI11 = 1 makes the chip take DI06:00 (DI10:00 in the Auto modes); with DI11 = 0 it keeps the previous values. DI10 restarts an Auto sequence; DI06 is the range; DI05 powers down; DI04 makes the next reply carry the GPIO levels instead of the channel address; DI03:00 are the GPIO output levels. The driver always sends DI11 = 1 with the configured range and levels, and DI04 = DI05 = 0 except where a call needs them. The word out has the channel address in DO15:12 and the 12-bit result, straight binary, in DO11:00 ( reg::ReplyAddress() , reg::ReplyCode() ). It is the conversion of the input sampled at that frame's CS falling edge, which the multiplexer acquired during the frame before, which the frame before that chose: a channel chosen in frame N comes back in frame N + 2 (Figure 51). A range written in frame N applies from the same result. The first conversion after power-up or a reset is invalid (section 7.6). Modes ¶ Mode Channels Frames per result Manual The one each word names 3 for a new channel, then 1 for each repeat Auto-1 The channels of a 16-bit mask, ascending, wrapping 1, after 2 to enter Auto-2 Channel 0 up to a last channel, wrapping 1, after 2 to enter Entering an Auto mode from another mode restarts its sequence (sections 8.4.5 and 8.4.6). Writing the Auto-1 mask while in Auto-1 moves the chip on to the next enabled channel of the new mask; writing the Auto-2 last channel while in Auto-2 restarts it at channel 0. The chip keeps converting in its mode while a program register is written, and its replies stay valid. The chip has no way to read a register back. Alarms ¶ Each channel has a high and a low threshold of 10 bits, compared with the upper 10 bits of each result (Table 13): the two lowest bits of a code do not count. GPIO0 can be the "high or low" or the high alarm output and GPIO1 the low alarm output (TSSOP only), active high, set on the 12 th SCLK of the frame that converts the channel and cleared on the 10 th SCLK of the next (section 8.1). Programming a group of four channels takes the group frame, one frame per threshold and one frame to leave the sequence. docs.text: A result comes back two frames after its channel Figure description and sources Each column is one 16-bit frame, CS low for 16 SCLK cycles, left to right in time. In each panel the top row is the word the driver sends on SDI, the middle row the channel the multiplexer acquires during that frame, and the bottom row the reply on SDO: the conversion of the channel acquired in the frame before, sampled at this frame's CS falling edge, tagged with its address in DO15:12. In Manual mode (top) ReadChannel(4) selects channel 4 with a Manual word, sends a "continue" word and then the Manual word for channel 4 again (it carries the range once more), and keeps the third reply, whose address must be 4; the two replies before it still belong to the previous channel. In Auto-1 (bottom), entering the mode restarts the sequence at its first channel: with channels 2, 5 and 6 programmed, the first result arrives two frames after the Auto-1 word, and from then on every Auto-1 word without restart (DI11 = 1, the range again) returns the next channel of the sequence, so a pass costs one frame per channel. The timing is the datasheet's Figures 51 and 53; the frame counts come from ReadChannel(), readSelected(), scan() and collect() in src/ads7952.ipp. Drawn from: src/ads7952.ipp select() ; src/ads7952.ipp selectChecked() ; src/ads7952.ipp readSelected() ; src/ads7952.ipp scan() ; inc/ads7952_registers.hpp kContinue ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/frame-pipeline.py . Each frame is one 16-bit word in and one out, MSB first. The word in (DI15:00) has its command in DI15:12: DI15:12 Word Driver use 0000 Continue in the current mode; DI11:00 ignored (Table 7) Every frame that only reads 0001 Manual mode, next channel in DI10:07 (Table 1) ReadChannel() , ReadChannels() , the identity check 0010, 0011 Auto-1, Auto-2 mode (Tables 2, 5) ReadAuto1() , ReadAuto2() 0100 GPIO program register (Table 11) Start-up reset, GpioConfig 1000 Auto-1 program: the mask follows in the next frame (Table 3) SetAuto1Channels() 1001 Auto-2 program: last channel in DI09:06 (Table 6) SetAuto2LastChannel() 11bb Alarm program, group bb; thresholds follow (Table 13) SetAlarmThresholds() In a mode word, DI11 = 1 makes the chip take DI06:00 (DI10:00 in the Auto modes); with DI11 = 0 it keeps the previous values. DI10 restarts an Auto sequence; DI06 is the range; DI05 powers down; DI04 makes the next reply carry the GPIO levels instead of the channel address; DI03:00 are the GPIO output levels. The driver always sends DI11 = 1 with the configured range and levels, and DI04 = DI05 = 0 except where a call needs them. The word out has the channel address in DO15:12 and the 12-bit result, straight binary, in DO11:00 ( reg::ReplyAddress() , reg::ReplyCode() ). It is the conversion of the input sampled at that frame's CS falling edge, which the multiplexer acquired during the frame before, which the frame before that chose: a channel chosen in frame N comes back in frame N + 2 (Figure 51). A range written in frame N applies from the same result. The first conversion after power-up or a reset is invalid (section 7.6).

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( ads7952_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads7952.git external/driver-ads7952 git submodule update --init external/driver-ads7952 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-ads7952 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE ads7952::ads7952 ) ads7952::ads7952 is an alias of the ads7952 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect ADS7952_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver ADS7952_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-ads7952 -B build-ads7952 cmake --install build-ads7952 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( ads7952 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE ads7952::ads7952 ) The target is ads7952::ads7952 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated ads7952_version.h go to include/ads7952/inc/ , the template implementation to include/ads7952/src/ads7952.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-ads7952) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-ads7952 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads7952.git components/ads7952 ads7952 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml ads7952 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : ads7952 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ads7952.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES ads7952 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/ads7952_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into ads7952_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = ads7952 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Status and limitations ¶ What this driver has and has not been shown to do, so you can decide whether it is ready for your use. Status ¶ Version 0.1.0, not released On hardware Not verified on hardware. No board has run this driver yet; Before you depend on it lists the bench steps Tested against A protocol model of the four parts ( Testing and CI ), a fuzzer and the quality gates Assurance level high (Kokeb Labs handbook): not qualified for use in a safety function Parts ADS7950, ADS7951, ADS7952, ADS7953 (12-bit). The 10-bit ADS7954 to ADS7957 and 8-bit ADS7958 to ADS7961 share the frame format but are not supported Design choices and their datasheet basis ¶ Each choice below closes a failure that a real bus or board can produce. It cites the datasheet section it rests on; the model has the fault, and a test pins the behaviour. The identity check needs SDI to reach the chip. After power-up or a reset the chip runs Manual mode on channel 0 (sections 8.4.1 and 8.4.3), and a frame whose DI15:12 are 0000 keeps the current mode and channel (section 8.4.7, Table 7). A chip that never receives SDI reads all zeros and so answers channel 0 frame after frame, with codes that look like data; a MISO stuck low reads as channel 0 too, and a MISO carrying a fixed pattern returns one address. The identity check selects two channels whose addresses differ in every bit and demands the first twice and then the second (a, a, b) ( Contract ). A chip left scanning an Auto-1 sequence of exactly those two channels answers a, b in turn but never repeats an address, so it fails as well. The model has the faults ( deaf_sdi , Miso::StuckLow , Miso::Pattern with 0x0E83, Miso::FloatHigh , Miso::EchoMosi ); the tests and the fuzzer cover them. A result belongs to the channel in its reply, two frames after the select. The datasheet puts a channel's result in frame N + 2 (section 8.4.4, Figure 51), not N + 1. The driver tracks the pipeline and checks the address of every result it returns ( ChannelMismatch , SequenceMismatch ), and of the replies a new select or an Auto entry discards: from a settled Manual channel they must carry that channel. A reset behind the driver's back is detected where a reply can show it, and the driver then stops. A reset (a brown-out) puts every register back to its reset value: Manual mode on channel 0, Range 1 (section 8.4.3, Table 1), every GPIO an input with no alarm function (Table 11), the alarm thresholds to all ones and all zeros (section 8.5.3); the first conversion after it is invalid (section 7.6). The chip has no flag for it, so its only sign is a reply from channel 0 where the driver expects another channel. That is DeviceReset . After it, and after any ChannelMismatch or SequenceMismatch (a lost frame and a reset cannot always be told apart), the driver is uninitialised: every call returns NotInitialized until EnsureInitialized() resets the chip, programs every register in the order of section 8.4.3 and discards the invalid first conversion. The driver never goes on writing from a copy of a configuration the chip has lost. This is the fail-safe choice over reprogramming on its own: an alarm interlock that a reset disarmed is reported to the application, which decides when to re-arm it. Every mode word carries the range. A mode word changes the range only with DI11 = 1 (Tables 1 and 2). Every mode word the driver sends has DI11 = 1 and the configured range, and so does the frame that returns a ReadChannel() result (the Manual word for the same channel, not a "continue" word, at the same frame count), so the range is back at the next read after a reset the driver did not see. The register reset at every start (DI09 of the GPIO program register, Table 11) also clears a GPIO2 left as the range input (DI07). ApplyConfig() writes every register. No register can be read back (section 8.4.2), so the driver's copy is never the reason to skip one: ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) writes the GPIO program register, both sequence program registers, every alarm threshold and the mode word (6 + 10 frames per alarm group, 36 on the ADS7952). A write whose transfer failed may have taken effect. A transfer the port reports as failed may still have clocked the frame into the chip. After a failed range, GPIO, sequence or alarm frame (or a read-back that did not confirm one), GetConfig() keeps the values last written successfully, never those of the failed write, and IsConfigUncertain() is true: the chip may hold either. Alarm thresholds in particular are never assumed set. ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) or EnsureInitialized() writes every register and clears it. The range and the GPIO levels also go out again with every mode word, select and read frame. Every pass of a sequence is checked. A reset returns the chip to Manual mode (section 8.4.3), and a corrupted frame that the chip reads as a mode word changes the mode (section 8.4.2.1). A pass whose addresses are not one turn of the sequence is SequenceMismatch (or DeviceReset for a reply from channel 0 out of turn), and the driver must be started again, which programs the sequence and restarts it at its first channel (section 8.4.5). Only EnsureInitialized() probes. SDO is driven only while CS is low: it goes to 3-state after the 16 th SCLK falling edge and when CS goes high (section 8.1; t d3 and t d4 , section 7.9). With the chip unpowered or unplugged, MISO floats to whatever the board pulls it to. The constructor does no I/O; call EnsureInitialized() from an explicit attach path, once the board is known to be powered. One LSB is full scale / 4096. Table 8 makes code 4095 full scale less one LSB. CodeToMicrovolts() divides by 4096; a division by 4095 would read 0.024 % high. The port reports every bus error. Transfer() returns bool , and the SpiPort concept rejects a port whose transfer returns void : a port that cannot report a failure would turn every failed transfer into a frame of data. The Auto-1 mask is written once. The program register keeps its value until power-down, reset or reprogramming, and Auto-1 may be left and entered again without disturbing it (section 8.4.1). The driver writes the mask (two frames, Table 3) only when it changes, and a running sequence costs k frames per pass. A program sequence is always closed. Auto-1 programming takes two frames, and the chip takes the second frame's word as the mask whatever it holds (section 8.4.5, Figure 54 and Table 3). An alarm sequence stays open until a frame with the exit bit DI12 = 1, and every word until then is taken as a threshold (section 8.5.3, Table 13). After a failed frame inside a sequence the driver therefore repeats the mask or closes the alarm sequence, and every start-up opens with two frames that end any sequence (found by the bus-fault sweep and the fuzzer). Limits of the design ¶ A reset at any moment the chip rests on channel 0 in Manual mode shows in no reply. Channel 0 is the power-on channel (section 8.4.3), so its replies carry the same address before and after. That covers more than a loop of ReadChannel(0) : in any mix of reads, a reset while the chip rests on channel 0 (after a read of channel 0, or a ReadChannels() list that ends with it) is followed by a select from channel 0, which looks the same, and a ReadChannels() list or a TraceFrames() selects before it reads. Such a reset may never be seen. Two results after it are wrong: the invalid first conversion (section 7.6) and one acquired in Range 1 before the next read frame sent the range again. Elsewhere the one reply in flight across a reset can still be returned when the chip keeps it (right address, invalid code); the next reply is DeviceReset . An Auto-1 sequence of channel 0 alone, or Auto-2 ending at channel 0, returns up to three passes after a reset (the same two wrong results) before the chip, back in Auto-1 with the reset sequence, shows another channel. Until the configuration is written again, the alarm function and thresholds stay lost. Where GPIO0 or GPIO1 alarms feed an interlock, use these mitigations: set Config::park_channel (opt-in) to a channel other than 0. After each ReadChannel(0) the chip then rests on that channel (one frame more; 4 frames per repeated ReadChannel(0) instead of 1), and the next read sees a reset as DeviceReset ; call ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) (36 frames on the ADS7952) at the rate the interlock's reaction time needs, or Deinitialize() and EnsureInitialized() ; declare a Config::monitor on a channel other than 0 and call CheckScale() (a Range 1 reading is DeviceReset ). Bench step 5 confirms the detection on hardware. - A frame lost before the chip, but reported as sent, is not always caught. A lost range or GPIO word leaves the chip on the old setting until the next mode word; only a known input shows it, which is what Config::monitor and CheckScaleCode() are for. A MISO line that fails after start-up into a fixed word whose address happens to match the channel being read is taken as that channel's result. Both need a board-level check. - The datasheet does not say whether the word sent in the frame that performs a register reset is obeyed. Table 11 says only that the reset happens in the next CS frame. The driver sends a "continue" word there, which is harmless either way, and the model ignores that frame's word. Bench step 1 below runs the start-up that depends on it. Handbook rules this chip gives no handle for ¶ Some driver rules of the handbook need a feature the ADS795x does not have. Each is met as far as the chip allows, and the rest is stated here: Rule What the chip has What the driver does Clear-on-read flags in a latch (KB-CPP-119) No clear-on-read or write-1-to-clear flag: a reply is an address (or the GPIO levels) and a code; the alarm outputs are pins, set on the 12 th SCLK falling edge of a frame and cleared on the 10 th of the next (section 8.1) No latch. GetLastReply() keeps the last raw reply Wait for the chip's ready indication (KB-CPP-124) No ready, busy or ID bit; only the power-up time after a reset or wake-up (section 7.6) Waits the power-up time, discards the invalid first conversion, and treats the identity check, which the chip must answer frame by frame, as the proof that it is up A stuck line's reply is never data (KB-CPP-116) 0x0000 is also channel 0 converting 0 V, and 0xFFFF channel 15 converting full scale (ADS7953) At start-up both fail the identity check ( DeviceIdMismatch , NoDevice ). After start-up a MISO stuck low reads as channel 0 at code 0: a scan of two or more channels catches it (the addresses must step), a single read of channel 0 cannot. When code 0 on channel 0 matters, confirm it: CheckScale() on a monitor channel other than 0 fails on a MISO stuck low (its reply address is wrong) Register read-back (KB-CPP-122, KB-ARCH-041) No register can be read back except the GPIO levels; the range is not reported (section 8.4.2) Registers are written whole from the driver's copy; Verify::ReadBack reads the GPIO levels or scans the new sequence, and the scale monitor witnesses the range What the model cannot show ¶ The model is written from the datasheet, by the same reading as the driver. It cannot show: whether the GPIO levels latched on a CS falling edge already include outputs refreshed on that edge (the driver's Verify::ReadBack reads one frame later, so it does not depend on it); what the chip does with the word of the frame after an alarm exit bit (the model ignores it, the driver sends a "continue" word there); analog behaviour: acquisition and settling at your SCLK and source impedance, noise, the input range near +VA; electrical timing: the CS high time, SDO delays, a slow MISO edge at 4 MHz on a long link. Before you depend on it ¶ Run these on your board, with the driver behind the code that owns it, and record the result below: Board plugged: EnsureInitialized() returns Ok in 13 frames (logic analyser on CS: 13 CS pulses), 16 with a scale monitor declared ( Config::monitor ). Board unplugged: NoDevice (last reply 0xFFFF) or DeviceIdMismatch , never Ok . SDI disconnected: DeviceIdMismatch . TraceFrames(ch, words) with six words, on a channel ch with a known input: the address nibble of words[2] onwards is ch and the code matches the input; ReadChannel(ch) returns the same code. SetAuto1Channels(mask, Verify::ReadBack) with your k-channel list, then 1,000 ReadAuto1() passes: each Ok , k frames each after the first (count CS pulses), the codes equal to a polled read of the same channels within 1 to 2 LSB. Power-cycle the analog board while ReadAuto1() runs, and again while ReadChannel(3) runs in a loop: DeviceReset (or SequenceMismatch / ChannelMismatch ), IsInitialized() false and NotInitialized from every call, then Ok again after EnsureInitialized() , with the scale monitor's code back in its window (the range restored) and the GPIO0 alarm tripping again on an input above its threshold. Repeat with ReadChannel(0) and check that ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) re-arms the alarm; repeat once more with Config::park_channel set: the loop of ReadChannel(0) returns DeviceReset within two calls of the power cycle. Scope SCLK and CS at 4 MHz: 16 clocks per frame, CS high between frames. With the monitor declared: lift REFP (or the monitor resistor) and start: ScaleMismatch . With GPIO2 as the range input, hold it at the other level: RangeMismatch . Measure +VA at the chip under full load (every load on the supply running) and record the minimum: it is va_min_mv , and Range 2 needs it at 2 x VREF or more (5000 with a 2.5 V reference). docs.text: Each choice below closes a failure that a real bus or board can produce. It cites the datasheet section it rests on; the model has the fault, and a test pins the behaviour. The identity check needs SDI to reach the chip. After power-up or a reset the chip runs Manual mode on channel 0 (sections 8.4.1 and 8.4.3), and a frame whose DI15:12 are 0000 keeps the current mode and channel (section 8.4.7, Table 7). A chip that never receives SDI reads all zeros and so answers channel 0 frame after frame, with codes that look like data; a MISO stuck low reads as channel 0 too, and a MISO carrying a fixed pattern returns one address. The identity check selects two channels whose addresses differ in every bit and demands the first twice and then the second (a, a, b) ( Contract ). A chip left scanning an Auto-1 sequence of exactly those two channels answers a, b in turn but never repeats an address, so it fails as well. The model has the faults ( deaf_sdi , Miso::StuckLow , Miso::Pattern with 0x0E83, Miso::FloatHigh , Miso::EchoMosi ); the tests and the fuzzer cover them. A result belongs to the channel in its reply, two frames after the select. The datasheet puts a channel's result in frame N + 2 (section 8.4.4, Figure 51), not N + 1. The driver tracks the pipeline and checks the address of every result it returns ( ChannelMismatch , SequenceMismatch ), and of the replies a new select or an Auto entry discards: from a settled Manual channel they must carry that channel. A reset behind the driver's back is detected where a reply can show it, and the driver then stops. A reset (a brown-out) puts every register back to its reset value: Manual mode on channel 0, Range 1 (section 8.4.3, Table 1), every GPIO an input with no alarm function (Table 11), the alarm thresholds to all ones and all zeros (section 8.5.3); the first conversion after it is invalid (section 7.6). The chip has no flag for it, so its only sign is a reply from channel 0 where the driver expects another channel. That is DeviceReset . After it, and after any ChannelMismatch or SequenceMismatch (a lost frame and a reset cannot always be told apart), the driver is uninitialised: every call returns NotInitialized until EnsureInitialized() resets the chip, programs every register in the order of section 8.4.3 and discards the invalid first conversion. The driver never goes on writing from a copy of a configuration the chip has lost. This is the fail-safe choice over reprogramming on its own: an alarm interlock that a reset disarmed is reported to the application, which decides when to re-arm it. Every mode word carries the range. A mode word changes the range only with DI11 = 1 (Tables 1 and 2). Every mode word the driver sends has DI11 = 1 and the configured range, and so does the frame that returns a ReadChannel() result (the Manual word for the same channel, not a "continue" word, at the same frame count), so the range is back at the next read after a reset the driver did not see. The register reset at every start (DI09 of the GPIO program register, Table 11) also clears a GPIO2 left as the range input (DI07). ApplyConfig() writes every register. No register can be read back (section 8.4.2), so the driver's copy is never the reason to skip one: ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) writes the GPIO program register, both sequence program registers, every alarm threshold and the mode word (6 + 10 frames per alarm group, 36 on the ADS7952). A write whose transfer failed may have taken effect. A transfer the port reports as failed may still have clocked the frame into the chip. After a failed range, GPIO, sequence or alarm frame (or a read-back that did not confirm one), GetConfig() keeps the values last written successfully, never those of the failed write, and IsConfigUncertain() is true: the chip may hold either. Alarm thresholds in particular are never assumed set. ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) or EnsureInitialized() writes every register and clears it. The range and the GPIO levels also go out again with every mode word, select and read frame. Every pass of a sequence is checked. A reset returns the chip to Manual mode (section 8.4.3), and a corrupted frame that the chip reads as a mode word changes the mode (section 8.4.2.1). A pass whose addresses are not one turn of the sequence is SequenceMismatch (or DeviceReset for a reply from channel 0 out of turn), and the driver must be started again, which programs the sequence and restarts it at its first channel (section 8.4.5). Only EnsureInitialized() probes. SDO is driven only while CS is low: it goes to 3-state after the 16 th SCLK falling edge and when CS goes high (section 8.1; t d3 and t d4 , section 7.9). With the chip unpowered or unplugged, MISO floats to whatever the board pulls it to. The constructor does no I/O; call EnsureInitialized() from an explicit attach path, once the board is known to be powered. One LSB is full scale / 4096. Table 8 makes code 4095 full scale less one LSB. CodeToMicrovolts() divides by 4096; a division by 4095 would read 0.024 % high. The port reports every bus error. Transfer() returns bool , and the SpiPort concept rejects a port whose transfer returns void : a port that cannot report a failure would turn every failed transfer into a frame of data. The Auto-1 mask is written once. The program register keeps its value until power-down, reset or reprogramming, and Auto-1 may be left and entered again without disturbing it (section 8.4.1). The driver writes the mask (two frames, Table 3) only when it changes, and a running sequence costs k frames per pass. A program sequence is always closed. Auto-1 programming takes two frames, and the chip takes the second frame's word as the mask whatever it holds (section 8.4.5, Figure 54 and Table 3). An alarm sequence stays open until a frame with the exit bit DI12 = 1, and every word until then is taken as a threshold (section 8.5.3, Table 13). After a failed frame inside a sequence the driver therefore repeats the mask or closes the alarm sequence, and every start-up opens with two frames that end any sequence (found by the bus-fault sweep and the fuzzer).

docs.text: A reset at any moment the chip rests on channel 0 in Manual mode shows in no reply. Channel 0 is the power-on channel (section 8.4.3), so its replies carry the same address before and after. That covers more than a loop of ReadChannel(0) : in any mix of reads, a reset while the chip rests on channel 0 (after a read of channel 0, or a ReadChannels() list that ends with it) is followed by a select from channel 0, which looks the same, and a ReadChannels() list or a TraceFrames() selects before it reads. Such a reset may never be seen. Two results after it are wrong: the invalid first conversion (section 7.6) and one acquired in Range 1 before the next read frame sent the range again. Elsewhere the one reply in flight across a reset can still be returned when the chip keeps it (right address, invalid code); the next reply is DeviceReset . An Auto-1 sequence of channel 0 alone, or Auto-2 ending at channel 0, returns up to three passes after a reset (the same two wrong results) before the chip, back in Auto-1 with the reset sequence, shows another channel. Until the configuration is written again, the alarm function and thresholds stay lost. Where GPIO0 or GPIO1 alarms feed an interlock, use these mitigations: set Config::park_channel (opt-in) to a channel other than 0. After each ReadChannel(0) the chip then rests on that channel (one frame more; 4 frames per repeated ReadChannel(0) instead of 1), and the next read sees a reset as DeviceReset ; call ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) (36 frames on the ADS7952) at the rate the interlock's reaction time needs, or Deinitialize() and EnsureInitialized() ; declare a Config::monitor on a channel other than 0 and call CheckScale() (a Range 1 reading is DeviceReset ). Bench step 5 confirms the detection on hardware. - A frame lost before the chip, but reported as sent, is not always caught. A lost range or GPIO word leaves the chip on the old setting until the next mode word; only a known input shows it, which is what Config::monitor and CheckScaleCode() are for. A MISO line that fails after start-up into a fixed word whose address happens to match the channel being read is taken as that channel's result. Both need a board-level check. - The datasheet does not say whether the word sent in the frame that performs a register reset is obeyed. Table 11 says only that the reset happens in the next CS frame. The driver sends a "continue" word there, which is harmless either way, and the model ignores that frame's word. Bench step 1 below runs the start-up that depends on it.

docs.text: Some driver rules of the handbook need a feature the ADS795x does not have. Each is met as far as the chip allows, and the rest is stated here: Rule What the chip has What the driver does Clear-on-read flags in a latch (KB-CPP-119) No clear-on-read or write-1-to-clear flag: a reply is an address (or the GPIO levels) and a code; the alarm outputs are pins, set on the 12 th SCLK falling edge of a frame and cleared on the 10 th of the next (section 8.1) No latch. GetLastReply() keeps the last raw reply Wait for the chip's ready indication (KB-CPP-124) No ready, busy or ID bit; only the power-up time after a reset or wake-up (section 7.6) Waits the power-up time, discards the invalid first conversion, and treats the identity check, which the chip must answer frame by frame, as the proof that it is up A stuck line's reply is never data (KB-CPP-116) 0x0000 is also channel 0 converting 0 V, and 0xFFFF channel 15 converting full scale (ADS7953) At start-up both fail the identity check ( DeviceIdMismatch , NoDevice ). After start-up a MISO stuck low reads as channel 0 at code 0: a scan of two or more channels catches it (the addresses must step), a single read of channel 0 cannot. When code 0 on channel 0 matters, confirm it: CheckScale() on a monitor channel other than 0 fails on a MISO stuck low (its reply address is wrong) Register read-back (KB-CPP-122, KB-ARCH-041) No register can be read back except the GPIO levels; the range is not reported (section 8.4.2) Registers are written whole from the driver's copy; Verify::ReadBack reads the GPIO levels or scans the new sequence, and the scale monitor witnesses the range

It cannot show: whether the GPIO levels latched on a CS falling edge already include outputs refreshed on that edge (the driver's Verify::ReadBack reads one frame later, so it does not depend on it); what the chip does with the word of the frame after an alarm exit bit (the model ignores it, the driver sends a "continue" word there); analog behaviour: acquisition and settling at your SCLK and source impedance, noise, the input range near +VA; electrical timing: the CS high time, SDO delays, a slow MISO edge at 4 MHz on a long link.
